title: Apply for a general construction induction card (white card)
summary: Find out if you need and how to apply for a general construction induction card (white card).
intro:
You'll need a general construction induction card, commonly called a white card, if any of the following apply:

Note: A white card can be used in any Australian state or territory.
what_you_need: A construction induction training course from a registered training organisation (RTO)

how_to_steps.text: Follow the prompts to find an RTO.
send your application to SafeWork NSW
give you a statement of training that you can use for 60 days (until you receive your white card from SafeWork NSW).

more_info.text: If you have a construction induction card from another Australian state or territory, you can use it in NSW – check to make sure your card is valid.
Your white card will usually arrive within 30 days. If you do not receive your card, call 13 10 50.
You need to take part in a safety induction each time you work on a new construction site.
Always carry your white card with you when you're at work.
Once you receive your white card, you can access it digitally through the Service NSW app.
You can verify NSW white cards online.

faqs.q: Can a white card be used outside of NSW?
faqs.a: Yes, a white card can be used in any Australian state or territory.

faqs.q: What is the minimum age to hold a white card?
faqs.a: You must be aged 14 or over.

faqs.q: What do I need to apply for a white card?
faqs.a: You need proof of identity, a construction induction training course from a registered training organisation (RTO), and payment for the course.
